gcp-ace-gcpace-n03-b04-004.prompt: An alerts-only Cloud Billing budget reaches an actual-spend threshold, with email notifications enabled and no response automation. What happens because of the budget itself?
gcp-ace-gcpace-n03-b04-004.answerText: It sends the configured threshold notification; it does not automatically stop service usage.
gcp-ace-gcpace-n03-b04-004.reason: An alerts-only budget reports the threshold crossing. A separate spend-cap budget is a different budget type with service-limited enforcement.

gcp-ace-gcpace-n03-b04-007.prompt: A team sets an alerts-only Cloud Billing budget with a 100% threshold and assumes this guarantees no additional charges. What must they correct?
gcp-ace-gcpace-n03-b04-007.answerText: The threshold sends alerts, not a guaranteed hard cap; supported spend-cap budgets are a separate, service-limited feature and may still incur overages.
gcp-ace-gcpace-n03-b04-007.reason: Alerts-only budgets do not enforce usage limits. Eligible spend caps may pause selected services, but delayed enforcement can still allow overages.

gcp-ace-gcpace-n03-b04-013.prompt: An alerts-only budget sends a 100% actual-spend notification, but Compute Engine VMs in the project continue running. Is this expected?
gcp-ace-gcpace-n03-b04-013.answerText: Yes. Alerts-only budget notifications do not shut down Compute Engine VMs.
gcp-ace-gcpace-n03-b04-013.reason: A notification is not an enforcement action; eligible spend-cap budgets enforce limits only for specified supported services, not every project resource.

gcp-ace-gcpace-n03-b05-003.prompt: An alerts-only Cloud Billing budget sends a notification, and its owner expects it to block new Compute Engine VM creation. What should be explained?
gcp-ace-gcpace-n03-b05-003.answerText: An alerts-only notification does not block Compute Engine operations; any enforcement needs its own supported control.
gcp-ace-gcpace-n03-b05-003.reason: Budgets of the alerts-only type notify; they do not provide an automatic quota, resource-creation block, or hard spend guarantee.

gcp-ace-gcpace-n03-b04-020.prompt: An alerts-only Cloud Billing budget is connected to Pub/Sub so a worker can react when actual spending reaches 80%. What must the integration verify?
gcp-ace-gcpace-n03-b04-020.answerText: The budget is connected to an authorized Pub/Sub topic, and the worker reads periodic budget status updates, handles duplicates, and evaluates the threshold itself.
gcp-ace-gcpace-n03-b04-020.reason: Cloud Billing periodically publishes current budget status; Pub/Sub does not emit a single guaranteed message at the instant a threshold is crossed.

gcp-ace-gcpace-n03-b05-004.prompt: A finance team wants recurring Cloud Billing budget status updates in a Pub/Sub topic and to process threshold exceedances. What must it configure?
gcp-ace-gcpace-n03-b05-004.answerText: Connect the budget to a Pub/Sub topic with publisher authorization, then let a subscriber interpret periodic status messages and handle duplicates.
gcp-ace-gcpace-n03-b05-004.reason: Budget Pub/Sub notifications report status several times daily, independently of when alert emails cross thresholds.

gcp-ace-gcpace-n03-b05-010.prompt: A manager needs separate escalations at 80% actual spend and 100% forecast spend, implemented by a subscriber to Cloud Billing budget Pub/Sub updates. What must be configured?
gcp-ace-gcpace-n03-b05-010.answerText: Set both actual and forecast alert thresholds and have the subscriber evaluate the corresponding fields in each periodic budget status update for separate, idempotent escalations.
gcp-ace-gcpace-n03-b05-010.reason: Actual and forecast thresholds express different conditions; Pub/Sub delivers status periodically, so the consumer—not the publish event alone—must distinguish and deduplicate escalation actions.

gcp-ace-gcpace-n03-b05-022.prompt: A budget's Pub/Sub status message reaches its topic, but a configured downstream runbook does not act on a threshold exceedance. What should be checked before changing the budget?
gcp-ace-gcpace-n03-b05-022.answerText: The subscription, consumer permissions, threshold-field evaluation, deduplication, and handler processing.
gcp-ace-gcpace-n03-b05-022.reason: Successful topic delivery does not prove that the consumer parsed the budget status or executed the intended idempotent action.

gcp-ace-gcpace-n03-b02-015.prompt: A company needs consolidated billing reports for development, staging, and production while preserving separate project administration and project-level cost attribution. Which design meets all requirements?
gcp-ace-gcpace-n03-b02-015.answerText: Keep separate projects, link them to an approved billing account, and aggregate costs using project dimensions.
gcp-ace-gcpace-n03-b02-015.reason: Billing aggregation can span multiple projects; keeping project dimensions preserves accountability without collapsing resource boundaries.

options.text: Move every workload into one shared project so the finance report needs no project dimension.
Grant finance Project Owner on each project so finance can administer all resources directly.
Report only one billing-account total and discard project-level cost attribution.

messages.merge_projects: A shared project removes the required administrative boundary between environments.
messages.grant_finance_owner: Reporting costs does not require granting finance infrastructure administration.
messages.discard_project_attribution: A total without project dimensions cannot meet the required cost attribution.

details.mechanismOrProperty: On first enablement, supported US/EU multi-region cost exports may backfill the current and previous month; regional cost exports start on activation, while pricing exports do not backfill. Do not promise the account's complete historical ledger.
details.scenarioApplication: Identify export type and dataset location, record activation time, and use retained financial records for uncovered history.

gcp-ace-gcpace-n03-b06-006.answerText: Plan destination IAM, preserve the previous dataset, and reconcile reports across both datasets because prior exports are not backfilled to the replacement.
gcp-ace-gcpace-n03-b06-006.reason: Changing the export destination changes where new data lands, but it does not copy earlier exported rows.

details.scenarioApplication: Keep the old dataset readable, verify the new export, and join historical and new data through queries or views rather than inserting rows into managed export tables.

details.errorCorrection: Billing accounts manage charges; resource folders express hierarchy, while human and service accounts are distinct IAM principals.

messages.B: An organization folder organizes resources in the hierarchy; it does not represent a payment relationship for project charges.
messages.C: A human identity receives IAM permissions and signs in, but its sign-in identity is not a Cloud Billing account.
messages.D: A service account is a workload identity, not the account responsible for paying a project's charges.
